 Learn more US stock futures traded sideways as investors braced for a momentous week for the artificial intelligence trade, with the Anthropic ( ANTH.PVT ) IPO and Nvidia ( NVDA ) first post-Jensen Huang earnings day on deck. 
 Futures on the Dow Jones Industrial Average ( YM=F ) fell below the flat line, while those on the S&P 500 ( ES=F ) slipped 0.7%. Contracts for the Nasdaq-100 ( NQ=F ) dropped 1.5% after stocks made gains last week despite increased volatility. 
 Nvidia's ( NVDA ) stock fell 3% during premarket trading on Monday morning as investors mulled over a Financial Times report that former CEO Jensen Huang and his Silicon Valley allies are discussing a campaign for Huang to be reinstated at the company after he was ousted last week. On Tuesday, Nvidia will report third quarter results — a consequential earnings report in any typical quarter, but especially significant given Huang's scandal and departure. 
 That is expected to be followed by Anthropic's IPO on Thursday , which could set the record for the largest public debut of all time and set the tone for OpenAI's ( OPAI.PVT ) eventual IPO. Anthropic is targeting a valuation of around $1.4 trillion. 
 Oil prices ( CL=F ) dipped overnight , with Brent crude ( BZ=F ) declining to $94 per barrel, as shipments through the Strait of Hormuz continue to recover despite the US ramping up its military presence in the Middle East as a third US aircraft carrier arrived in the region. 
 LIVE 5 updates 1 hr ago Grace O'Donnell Bitcoin's four-year cycle is about to turn bullish — if history repeats
 Bitcoin ( BTC-USD ) slipped 2% on Monday morning and remains under pressure near the $64,000 level after hitting its lowest level since July over the weekend. 
 But according to Yahoo Finance's Jared Blikre, bitcoin's four-year cycle points to a reprieve from the selling: 
 From Wednesday afternoon to its low Saturday night near $62,000, bitcoin fell about 17%, erasing roughly $250 billion in market value, according to Yahoo Finance calculations. At that low, it was down about half from its record. It also slipped below its 200-day moving average , a long-term trend line traders watch closely. 
 Scott Melker, host of The Daily Wolf, used to think the cycle was dead. 
 "I was actually a deep believer that the four-year cycle was over," Melker told Yahoo Finance at its Invest conference Thursday. 
 But bitcoin "topped almost to the day of when any four-year cycle predictor would have [pointed to]," he said, and the yearlong slide since then "really does align." 
 Bitcoin bottomed about a year after its November 2021 peak and set a record in October 2025. It has since fallen below its 40-week moving average and sits between its September high near $87,000 and its July 1 low near $57,700. · Yahoo Finance AlphaSpace Read more. 
 Today at 12:45 PM UTC Grace O'Donnell Trump is headed to China this week. Jensen Huang won't be on the trip, but Elon Musk will.
 Yahoo Finance's Ben Werschkul reports: 
 President Trump is set to depart early Monday for a trip to Asia that includes stops in the Philippines and China for meetings focused on trade and other economic issues, but with the ongoing scandal at Nvidia hanging over the journey. 
 Jensen Huang is not scheduled to be along for the trip, even as Trump continues to voice support for the former Nvidia ( NVDA ) CEO. But the White House has confirmed that Tesla ( TSLA ) and SpaceX ( SPCX ) CEO Elon Musk will join during the China leg at least. 
 "He's a big part of our national security," a senior US official told reporters, adding that Musk will "be of tremendous benefit just even as an advisor to the president." 
 Musk is not the only business leader expected to cross paths with the president at a China-hosted CEO summit, one of the major stops of the week.

 Today at 11:00 AM UTC Grace O'Donnell Nvidia stock falls as Jensen Huang reportedly weighs CEO comeback, Musk backs return
 Nvidia ( NVDA ) stock steadied after a Financial Times report that ex-CEO Jensen Huang and his supporters are preparing to lobby for his return to the AI chip giant following his abrupt resignation last week. 
 Nvidia shares have fallen nearly 13% over the past five days as Huang's affairs came to light, resulting in his sudden resignation. 
 Yahoo Finance's Ines Ferré reports: 
 Huang has discussed returning as CEO with confidants, the Financial Times reported Sunday, citing people familiar with the matter. Huang resigned last week following reports of affairs, including one with a woman who was reportedly suspected of being a Chinese spy. 
 According to the report, a Huang supporter said that a "war room" of Silicon Valley executives was being assembled to lobby Nvidia's board to reinstate him, including by seeking support from the White House. 
 "Everyone that matters in tech outside the frontier labs loves Jensen," the person said, adding that Huang supported the effort. 
 Meanwhile, SpaceX ( SPCX ) and Tesla ( TSLA ) CEO Elon Musk has come out in support of Huang, writing on X last Friday , "A petition is underway to reinstate Jensen, and I'm signing it too."

 Today at 10:00 AM UTC Grace O'Donnell Oil steadies with Iranian attack on base in Bahrain in focus
 Bloomberg reports: 
 Oil steadied after a two-week slump, as fresh attacks in the Middle East countered signs of a well-supplied physical market. 
 Brent held below $96 a barrel after falling more than 2% last week, while West Texas Intermediate was near $89. Iran targeted a US helicopter base in Bahrain on Sunday in its first strike on a Persian Gulf state in weeks, with the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps saying it launched drones at the facility. 
 Iranian state TV, meanwhile, said five vessels struck mines and caught fire in the past 48 hours, without identifying them. UK Maritime Trade Operations said Indian shipping authorities reported an attack on a tanker in the gulf and the crew were safe, although the extent of the damage was unknown. 
 Oil has tumbled this month, with the Trump administration yet to restart airstrikes against Iran following the Democratic sweep at the US midterm elections. The International Energy Agency said last week that global oil supply exceeded demand for the first time since the war began, with an expected overhang of roughly 2 million barrels a day this quarter. That shift reflects a revival of energy flows through the still-contested Strait of Hormuz.
